title: Heston Blumenthal
wiki_lead:
Heston Marc Blumenthal   (; born 27 May 1966) is an English celebrity chef, television personality and food writer. His restaurants include the Fat Duck in Bray, Berkshire, a three-Michelin-star restaurant that was named the world's best by the World's 50 Best Restaurants in 2005.
Blumenthal is regarded as a pioneer of multi-sensory cooking, food pairing and flavour encapsulation. He came to public attention with unusual recipes such as bacon-and-egg ice cream and snail porridge. His recipes for triple-cooked chips and soft-centred Scotch eggs have been widely imitated. He has advocated a scientific approach to cooking, for which he has been awarded honorary degrees from the universities of Reading, Bristol and London and made an honorary fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry.
Blumenthal's public profile was boosted by a number of television series, most notably for Channel 4, as well as a product range for the Waitrose supermarket chain introduced in 2010. Blumenthal also owns Dinner, a two-Michelin-star restaurant in London, and a one-Michelin-star pub in Bray, the Hind's Head.
Blumenthal has attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, a condition he believes made him hyper-focused on his work, and bipolar disorder. He is an ambassador for the charity Bipolar UK.

Early life
Heston Marc Blumenthal was born in Shepherd's Bush, a suburb of West London, on 27 May 1966, to a Jewish businessman born in Southern Rhodesia and an English mother, a secretary, who converted to Judaism. His surname comes from a great-grandfather from Latvia and means "flowered valley" (or "bloom-dale") in German. His mother was often angry and unloving, calling him "useless" and "stupid", and never acknowledged his later achievements. Blumenthal was raised in Paddington, and attended Latymer Upper School in Hammersmith; St John's Church of England School in Lacey Green, Buckinghamshire; and John Hampden Grammar School, High Wycombe.
Blumenthal's interest in cooking began at the age of sixteen on a family holiday to Provence, France, when he was taken to the three-Michelin-star restaurant L'Oustau de Baumanière. He was inspired by the quality of the food and "the whole multi-sensory experience: the sound of fountains and cicadas, the heady smell of lavender, the sight of the waiters carving lamb at the table". When he learned to cook, he was influenced by the cookbook series Les recettes originales, with French chefs such as Alain Chapel.
Blumenthal left school at eighteen and began an apprenticeship at Raymond Blanc's Le Manoir aux Quat' Saisons, but left after a week's probation. Over the following ten years, he worked as a credit controller and repo man while teaching himself the French classical repertoire. A pivotal moment came when reading On Food and Cooking: the Science and Lore of the Kitchen by Harold McGee in the mid-1980s. grok_lead: Heston Marc Blumenthal OBE (born 27 May 1966) is a British celebrity chef, author, and television personality renowned for his scientific and experimental approach to gastronomy, blending molecular techniques with historical British cuisine at his acclaimed restaurants. Blumenthal, largely self-taught after being inspired by a trip to a French restaurant at age 16, opened his first venue, The Fat Duck in Bray, Berkshire, in 1995 from a converted pub, transforming it into a global destination for multi-sensory dining experiences that incorporate sound, smell, and unexpected flavors, such as nitro-scrambled egg and bacon ice cream. The restaurant earned its first Michelin star in 1999, a second in 2001, and a third in 2004, while being named the World's Best Restaurant by Restaurant magazine in 2005; it has retained three stars for over two decades, emphasizing Blumenthal's commitment to precision and innovation through collaborations with scientists like Harold McGee. In addition to The Fat Duck, Blumenthal operates Dinner by Heston Blumenthal in London's Mandarin Oriental Hotel, which opened in 2011 and holds two Michelin stars for its reimagined historical recipes, such as Meat Fruit inspired by 1500s techniques, and The Hind's Head, a more casual gastropub in Bray awarded one Michelin star. His contributions to British food earned him an OBE in 2006 for services to gastronomy, along with an honorary fellowship from the Royal Society of Chemistry in recognition of his food science advancements. Blumenthal has extended his influence through television series like Heston's Feasts (2009â2010), which explored historical banquets, and How to Cook Like Heston (2011), demystifying complex techniques for home cooks, as well as authoring best-selling books including The Big Fat Duck Cookbook (2008), which won James Beard Foundation awards for photography and design, and Heston Blumenthal at Home (2011). His work continues to emphasize sensory psychology and sustainability, collaborating on products like the Everdure barbecue range while maintaining a focus on evolving culinary traditions.
